## select()

```{r eval=FALSE}
? select
```


::: {.fragment}

Choose variables from a tibble.

**Usage**

... variables to select

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/06_dplyr_1.Rmd`.
:::

::: {.column width="49%"}
```{r}
tb
```

:::


::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/06_dplyr_1.Rmd`.

## Pipe `|>` 

* `x |> f(...)` is equivalent to `f(x,...)`.



::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="49%" .fragment}
```{r}
select(tb, a, b)
```
:::


::: {.column width="49%"}
```{r}
tb |> select(a, b)
```
:::
:::


::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/06_dplyr_1.Rmd`.
:::

---


## filter()

Return rows with matching conditions.


::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="49%"}
```{r}
tb
```
:::


::: {.column width="49%"}
```{r}
filter(tb, a >= 2, c == "y")
```
:::
:::


::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/06_dplyr_1.Rmd`.
:::

---


* `x |> f(...)` is equivalent to `f(x,...)`.


::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="49%"}
```{r}
filter(tb, a >= 2, c == "y")
```
:::


::: {.column width="49%"}
```{r}
tb |> filter(a >= 2, c == "y")
```
:::
:::


::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/06_dplyr_1.Rmd`.
:::

---


## Why use the pipe?


::: {.fragment}

Easier to read.

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="49%"}
```{r}
filter(tb, a >= 2, c == "y")
```
:::


::: {.column width="49%"}
```{r}
tb |> filter(a >= 2, c == "y")
```
:::
:::

:::


::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/06_dplyr_1.Rmd`.
:::

---


Chain multiple operations.

Suppose you want to do the following in sequence:

1. select columns a and c.
2. choose rows such that a>= 2 and c == "y".



::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="49%" .fragment}
```{r}
temp <- select(tb, a, c)
filter(temp, a >= 2, c == "y")
```
:::



::: {.column width="49%" .fragment}
```{r}
tb |>
    select(a, c) |>
    filter(a >= 2, c == "y")
```
:::
:::


::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/06_dplyr_1.Rmd`.
:::

---


## Native pipe `|>`

R has included the native pipe since version 4.1.0. It passes the result on the left to the function on the right.

```{r}
tb |>
    select(a, c) |>
    filter(a >= 2, c == "y")
```


::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/06_dplyr_1.Rmd`.
:::

---


The native pipe works without loading a package and composes naturally with tidyverse functions.



We will use `|>` throughout this course.


::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/06_dplyr_1.Rmd`.
:::

## Practice

From the bca dataset, generate a tibble of housing transactions satisfying the following:

- Add a new column called 'sale_year' containing the year of sale. (Use 'year()' function in 'lubridate' package.)
- Sold in 2017.
- Condo or townhouse (i.e., "Strata Res" in act_use_cat)
- Price is greater than 5 million dollars.
- Contain only the following columns: roll_num, sale_year, price, neigh_label.
- Sorted in the descending order of price.


::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/06_dplyr_1.Rmd`.
:::

---


## Read bca262.rds and store it as bca


::: {.fragment}

Restart R

```{r include=params$answers}
library(tidyverse)

bca <- read_rds("Data/bca262.rds")
```

:::


::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/06_dplyr_1.Rmd`.
:::

---


## Add a new column called 'sale_year' containing the year of sale. (Use 'year()' function in 'lubridate' package.), and store it as temp


::: {.fragment}

```{r include=params$answers}
library(lubridate)
temp <- bca |> mutate(sale_year = year(sale_date))
```

:::


::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/06_dplyr_1.Rmd`.
:::

---


## Keep only the rows satisfying the following conditions. Store it as temp.

- Sold in 2017.
- Condo or townhouse (i.e., "Strata Res" in act_use_cat)
- Price is greater than 5 million dollars.


::: {.fragment}

```{r include=params$answers}
temp <- temp |> filter(
    sale_year == 2017,
    act_use_cat == "Strata Res",
    price > 5000000
)
```

:::


::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/06_dplyr_1.Rmd`.
:::

---


## Keep only the following columns: roll_num, sale_year, price, neigh_label. Store it as temp.


::: {.fragment}

```{r include=params$answers}
temp <- temp |> select(roll_num, sale_year, price, neigh_label)
```

:::


::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/06_dplyr_1.Rmd`.
:::

---


## Sort in the descending order of price.


::: {.fragment}

```{r include=params$answers}
temp |> arrange(desc(price))
```

:::


::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/06_dplyr_1.Rmd`.
:::

---


## Rewrite all the codes using the pipes, without using a temp object!


```{r eval=FALSE, include=params$answers}
temp <- bca |> mutate(sale_year = year(sale_date))

temp <- temp |> filter(
    sale_year == 2017,
    act_use_cat == "Strata Res",
    price > 5000000
)

temp <- temp |>
    select(roll_num, sale_year, price, neigh_label)

temp |> arrange(desc(price))
```


::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/06_dplyr_1.Rmd`.
:::

---


```{r eval=FALSE, include=params$answers}
bca |>
    mutate(sale_year = year(sale_date)) |>
    filter(
        sale_year == 2017,
        act_use_cat == "Strata Res",
        price > 5000000
    ) |>
    select(roll_num, sale_year, price, neigh_label) |>
    arrange(desc(price))
```

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/06_dplyr_1.Rmd`.
:::
